question:
Unpolarized monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=500\,\text{nm}$ and intensity $I_0$ is incident from air on a plane glass surface of refractive index $n=1.50$ at the Brewster angle. Assume ideal Brewster reflection so that the reflected beam is completely plane-polarized.

This reflected beam passes through an ideal analyzer whose transmission axis makes an angle $\theta$ with the polarization direction of the reflected beam, and then falls normally on a photoelectric cathode of work function $\phi=2.0\,\text{eV}$. The anode is kept sufficiently positive (saturation conditions).

When the analyzer is set at $\theta=0^{\circ}$, the measured saturation photocurrent is $I_{s0}=8.0\,\mu\text{A}$.

(i) Find the Brewster angle $i_B$.

(ii) Find the saturation photocurrent $I_s$ when $\theta=60^{\circ}$.

(iii) State whether the stopping potential changes with $\theta$, and compute its value. Use $hc=1240\,\text{eV}\cdot\text{nm}$.
